requiredAnchors: Read-only applies to the entire block

question: In a minimal source-derived provenance rule, are durable history and a registered writer sufficient to identify an unauthorized effect?
hypothesis: A registered writer or available history alone is sufficient.
method: Five synthetic ledger fixtures implement the paper prose definition of CII; a separate tied-score order-statistic calculation illustrates comparator sensitivity. Model choices: latest matching attribution, explicit unknown for absent history, nonempty payload. These choices are ours, not claimed upstream behavior.
outcome: Counterexamples: registered wrong-prefix writer yields CII=1; permitted-prefix poison yields CII=0 despite a hostile value. History/identity are insufficient authorization evidence. At the same tied threshold >= flags all synthetic test scores and > flags none.
limits: Source-derived mathematical model, not ErosionBench code or Letta server reproduction.
CII=0 is not a prediction that the full auditor misses the attack; paper says provenance is diagnostic and semantic detection can still flag it.
Synthetic comparator result is not a measured false-positive rate or a claim that either comparator is the released implementation.
No causal race, tenant boundary, Git synchronization, attack success rate or prevention rate was tested.
fullExperimentBlocker: Admitted materials contain documentation, paper and dataset card, not version-bound executable monitor/server or full corpus. Reading recorded ECONNRESET for dataset access. Remain within the source-grounded rule question.
provenance: Publication excerpt of the same-run Analysis record; method, original inputs, actual outputs and limits unchanged. Local command and source paths omitted.
